messages.content: Hi! I'm Priya. I've been a high school chemistry teacher in Pittsburgh for six years and I'm starting to think about moving into data analysis.
That's a common and very doable switch. Teaching gives you strong communication skills. What draws you to data analysis?
I love the part of teaching where I grade lab reports and spot patterns in how students make mistakes. I already track all my class results in Google Sheets with pivot tables.
Pivot tables are a real head start. Next steps would usually be SQL and one visualization tool.
Please keep answers short and use bullet points. I read these on my phone between classes.

Got it.
- Learn SQL basics
- Pick Tableau or Power BI
- Build 2 small portfolio projects
I can only study on weekends. Weeknights are grading and lesson prep.

- Saturday: 3 hours of SQL
- Sunday: 2 hours on a project
- That pace gets you job-ready in about 6 months
Money is tight, so I'd rather not pay for a bootcamp. Free or cheap resources only.

- SQLBolt and Mode's SQL tutorial are free
- Tableau Public is free
- Kaggle has free datasets
Finished the first five SQLBolt lessons this weekend. Joins were confusing at first but I got there.

Nice progress.
- Joins are the hardest early concept
- Practice with two tables you know, like students and grades
My friend Dana works at a hospital analytics team and said healthcare data jobs are growing. That sounds meaningful to me.

- Healthcare analytics values domain knowledge
- Your science background helps
- Look at public CDC datasets for a project
I'd want to stay in Pittsburgh. My partner just started a job at CMU and we bought a house last year.

- UPMC and Highmark are big local healthcare employers
- Both hire analysts regularly
I looked at a few remote job listings and some of them pay more than UPMC. One of them was based in Austin.

- Remote roles can pay more but get more applicants
- Local roles can be easier to land as a first analyst job
Can you explain what a p-value is? It keeps coming up in job descriptions.

- A p-value is how surprising your data would be if there were no real effect
- Small p-value means the result is unlikely to be chance alone
- Example: if a new teaching method shows p = 0.01, that improvement is unlikely to be luck
That example with teaching really helped. Examples from school make things click for me.
Good to know. I'll use classroom examples when they fit.
Honestly I'm nervous. I'm 34 and everyone in the online forums seems to be 22.

- Career changers in their 30s are very common in analytics
- Six years of managing classrooms is real work experience
- Employers value maturity and communication
Thanks. I'm going to aim to apply for jobs next spring, after the school year ends in June.

- Start applying in March or April
- Leaves time for interviews before June
- Have 2 projects done by February
Need quick dinner ideas for this week. I'm vegetarian, and my partner eats everything.

- Black bean tacos with optional chicken on the side
- Veggie stir fry with tofu
- Pasta with roasted vegetables
Nothing with mushrooms please, I really can't stand the texture.

Noted, no mushrooms.
- Swap in zucchini or bell peppers
My sister's two kids are staying with us this weekend, so I need to buy juice boxes and snacks too.

- Apple slices and peanut butter
- Cheese sticks and crackers
- Popcorn for a movie night
Any ideas for keeping a 6 and 9 year old busy on Saturday in Pittsburgh?

- Carnegie Science Center
- Children's Museum of Pittsburgh
- Phipps Conservatory
The science center is perfect, I can nerd out about chemistry with them.
They have a great chemistry demo stage. Check the schedule online.
I'm training for the Pittsburgh half marathon in May. Can you suggest a beginner plan?

- 3 runs a week
- One long run on weekends, building 1 mile per week
- Rest days between runs
I run early mornings before school, around 5:30. It's the only quiet time I get.

- Keep weekday runs short, 25–35 minutes
- Save the long run for Sunday
My knee was sore after last week's run, so I took two days off.

- Rest was the right call
- If pain returns, see a physical therapist
- Check your shoes' mileage
I've been drinking way too much coffee. Trying to switch to green tea in the mornings.

- Green tea has about a third of the caffeine
- Try cutting one cup at a time
I was reading an article about Lisbon last night. The tiles and the food look amazing.
Lisbon is lovely. Spring and fall are the best times to visit.
Maybe someday. For now, any good audiobooks for long runs?

- Born to Run by Christopher McDougall
- The Martian by Andy Weir
- Atomic Habits by James Clear
I want my first portfolio project to use real data. I'm thinking about Pennsylvania hospital wait times.

- CMS publishes hospital data publicly
- Good fit for healthcare analytics roles
I'll do the analysis in SQL and the dashboard in Tableau Public. I decided against Power BI because it's Windows only and I use a Mac.

- Solid choice
- Tableau Public dashboards are easy to share in applications
I got stuck on a GROUP BY error for an hour today and almost gave up.

- Every column in SELECT must be grouped or aggregated
- That error trips up everyone
- Paste the query next time and I'll check it
Fixed it! The project is about half done. I found that rural hospitals have much longer ER waits.

- That's a strong, clear finding
- Lead your dashboard with it
Should I learn Python too, or is SQL plus Tableau enough for a first job?

- SQL + Tableau is enough for many entry roles
- Add basic Python with pandas after your second project
Ok. I'd rather go deep on SQL first than learn a little of everything.
Depth first is a good strategy. Window functions are the next step.
Update: I changed my mind about timing. I'm going to start applying in January instead of spring, because a UPMC analyst role I like opens then.

- January is doable
- Finish project one by December
- Tailor your resume to that role
Can you help me rewrite my resume summary later? I want it to sound confident but not fake.
Happy to. Bring your current version and the job description.
